Alex.confusing: The Meowfia payout: the 2x "Grudge" bonus on a winning throw was much larger than the rule text suggested, and the rules never said how the bonus is counted in the final score.
Alex.fun: Round 1, when I threw my three highest cards at the Farm player the table was about to eggsecute, as Meowfia. The doubled payout nearly decided the game.
Alex.change: Make the Meowfia double payout smaller, or cap it. One successful frame can outweigh the rest of the game.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I claimed that nobody visited me, which was a bad bluff as Turkey. I should have said I couldn't see visitors, and I nearly got eggsecuted for it.

Blair.confusing: How the scoring worked: the large bonus numbers (e.g. Alex's 42) weren't explained, and the Meowfia 2x stake only banking on the eggsecuted Farm player made throw sizing unclear.
Blair.fun: Round 3, when the three hugged players' stories pointed at Casey and I could confidently throw high cards and bank 29 points.
Blair.change: Make the end-of-game scoring bonus visible during play, so players can judge how the standings affect their risk.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw two 9+ cards at Ellis on a thin read and lost them. I should have thrown low cards or kept them. As Meowfia in round 2 I also staked three big cards on Alex instead of a smaller stake.

Casey.confusing: How the "Grudge" doubling worked in round 1 (my 26 points doubled to +26) versus the rules text. In round 2 I also couldn't tell who was lying about the Turkey.
Casey.fun: Round 1: getting Ellis eggsecuted with a fake Kookaburra claim and a doubled stake. It was a very satisfying bluff.
Casey.change: Let Meowfia see more clearly which Farm animals are in play, or how many of each exist. Judging a claim was hard without that.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I claimed Hawk and said I visited Drew, but the Floofer's hug victims all pointed at me. I would have accused someone first. In round 2 I should have thrown at Blair-like consensus instead of backing a losing vote on Alex, since Blair was my own partner.

Drew.confusing: How the banked-stake scoring works: Farm throws bank at full value when the target is Meowfia, so a big stake in round 3 was worth 38 points. Also unclear was whether a Turkey can see its visitors.
Drew.fun: Round 3, when Alex, Ellis and I all got hugged after visiting Casey. That pinned Casey as the Floofer and the table converged fast.
Drew.change: Show the scoring consequences of stake size more clearly, for example by listing each player's score pile total each round. Right now the ranking is hard to track, and one huge stake can decide the whole game.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I piled onto Ellis without checking the logic, and I lost a 9 for it. I should have questioned Alex's contradictory story and thrown a smaller stake, since Alex and Casey were the actual cats.

Ellis.confusing: How the Eagle's egg count interacted with other egg-layers in round 1. I couldn't tell whether the table's +1 arithmetic could be checked, and my own egg total got used against me.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when Alex, Drew and I all reported being hugged after visiting Casey. That pinned down the Floofer and the table agreed quickly.
Ellis.change: Give players a bit more information about what an egg count means. A simple per-role summary of who gains or loses eggs would make it easier to spot lies.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I claimed Eagle and said my +1 came from my own egg, and I accused Alex over the egg math. I should have said plainly that Alex's Owl egg and my Eagle egg would add to +2, and asked Casey directly about confusion before attacking.

Finley.confusing: How the score pile versus kept-card scoring worked, especially that a Meowfia stake only banks at 2x if the eggsecuted Farm player is the exact target. I also couldn't tell how large the end-of-game bonus would be.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when my Owl result exposed Alex's false "no visitors" claim. Then Blair's stalling got him eggsecuted and my throw banked 10 points.
Finley.change: Show the final-score bonus formula up front. I only saw the huge bonuses (42 for Alex) at the end, and they decided the game.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I threw 2 cards at Ellis on a loose read, and they were discarded. I should have kept them. In round 3, as Meowfia, I did nothing to help my side. I should have thrown a real stake at a Farm player, or used the Wink to disrupt the vote.

review.title: Alex Wins Quietly
review.headline: Alex lied his way to a runaway win while the table hunted others.
review.summary: Round 1 saw two cats (Alex and Casey) steer the table onto an honest Eagle, banking huge stakes and an early 60-point lead. Rounds 2 and 3 were clean Farm wins: Blair was caught after stalling on a role, and Casey was exposed by the Floofer hug trail. Nobody could catch the round 1 leader, and the game was effectively over after one round.

rounds.recap: Alex (Floofer) and Casey (Mouser) both lied smoothly. Casey claimed Kookaburra and Alex claimed Owl. Ellis the honest Eagle had a numbers dispute with Alex and was piled on. Ellis was eggsecuted as Farm, and the cats banked doubled stakes for 54 and 52 points.

Alex, the true Turkey, wrongly said nobody visited him, and the table piled on him. Finley's Owl report and Ellis's Kookaburra report confirmed him as Farm. Blair stalled on a role, then claimed Eagle, and Drew, Ellis and Finley switched to her. Blair was eggsecuted.

Casey the Floofer hugged Drew while three Farm players visited Casey and got hugged. That made Casey the obvious cat. Finley, the partner Mouser, stayed quiet and threw nothing. Casey was eggsecuted and Farm won.

highlights.text: Alex and Casey, secretly partners, both pushed Ellis, and Casey's heavy throw banked a large score off a Farm eggsecution.
Alex the honest Turkey claimed nobody visited him, which looked like a cat's cover story and nearly got him eggsecuted.
Drew, Ellis and Alex all visited Casey and got hugged, so the hug reports gave a clean deduction on the Floofer.
Finley, the hidden Mouser, stayed silent and threw zero cards at Drew to avoid being tied to Casey.

confusions.what: As Turkey he said nobody visited him and that anyone claiming otherwise was lying. A Turkey cannot see visitors.
Claimed Eagle, but his Eagle report listed Blair as the only visitor to Casey while also saying he visited Casey. He also counted Blair's visit as his +1 egg and never noticed his own visit.
Said Casey (a Kookaburra) would have been told they were confused. Blair also misread Ellis's +1 as ruling out Owl and Eagle both.
Claimed Kookaburra but said a visitor would confuse him, then argued Blair and Ellis both visiting would have caused confusion. This only held because he claimed Kookaburra falsely.
As Mouser he claimed Kookaburra and said he learned Alex was the Eagle. That is a mixed-up claim, since Mouser learns a role and Kookaburra also does, but he did not use his Wink.

worked: Floofer hug reports in round 3: several players visiting one target and all getting hugged gave a fair, readable deduction.
Egg counts and Owl/Kookaburra reports in round 2 let players verify Alex as Farm despite his bad claim.
Doubled stakes for Meowfia on a Farm eggsecution in round 1 made a big, real payoff for a successful bluff.
Stalling on a role in round 2 was punished, which made quick claims matter.
problems: Round 1 produced a 60-point swing for the cats (54 and 52 points) while Farm scored almost nothing. This decided the game in round 1, so rounds 2 and 3 had little tension. Fix: cap the doubling, or limit how much can bank per round.
Pile-ons form too fast. Three CAWs ended every day by beat 2 or 3, so there was little room for a real defense. Fix: raise the CAW threshold or require a later beat.
The Wink was held by Blair and Finley and never used. Wink never mattered, so Mouser felt weak.
The Floofer hugging visitors made a scapegoat in round 3 and left the cat team with no real play. Casey was almost certain to die.
Scores in the 50s to 90s dwarf nest value, so keeping cards for 1 point each almost never mattered next to staking high cards.
